title: CC Compute File
description: CLI-facing run descriptor bridging plugin manifests, compute manifests and the compute provider. Field names from cc-home/docs/07_compute-file.md. Note this file mixes snake_case and kebab-case ('execution-role', 'compute-manifests') within one document; all keys frozen.

name.description: User-defined name for the compute run.

queue.description: docker: must be 'docker-local'. awsbatch: the Batch queue name.

execution-role.description: awsbatch only. KEBAB-CASE, unlike every other provider field. Frozen.

profile.description: Named AWS credential profile resolved from the LOCAL aws credentials file. Meaningful only for the CLI; a plugin MUST NOT read it (STD-ENV-005).

plugins.description: Paths to plugin manifest files. Required for local Docker compute; required for awsbatch only at register time.
plugins.x-cc-known-divergence: Filesystem paths again, like dependencies. A reorganized directory tree changes what a compute file registers without any diff to the DAG's meaning.

compute-manifests.description: Unordered list of compute manifest files forming the event (DAG). Order comes from each manifest's dependencies, not from this array. KEBAB-CASE.

generator.description: Event generator. Absent means a single event with identifier 0.

delimiter.description: Single delimiter such as ',' or '\n'. The CLI accepts a file source only; other sources require code.

generator.x-cc-note: oneOf on the type discriminator, so a malformed generator names the failing branch instead of reporting three mismatches.

secrets-manager.description: In-memory secrets manager for the local Docker provider only. KEBAB-CASE.
secrets-manager.x-cc-security: STD-DATA-004: this block exists to hold values for local testing, which makes it the most likely place a real credential gets committed. It MUST contain placeholders only, and gitleaks runs over it in CI. Never copy a working local compute file into a repository.

perEventLoop.description: Key/value sets written into the environment once per loop iteration, multiplying the event count. An array of 1..N over start..end produces (end-start+1)*N jobs.
perEventLoop.x-cc-cost: This is the primary accidental-cost mechanism in the system: a 2000-event array with a 4-entry perEventLoop is 8000 jobs. Any tooling that estimates a run MUST multiply by perEventLoop length (STD-OPS-003).
